views.name: daily_web_device_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  day,
  pc,
  tablet,
  phone,
  (COALESCE(pc,0) + COALESCE(tablet,0) + COALESCE(phone,0)) AS total_devices
FROM web_devices
views.description: One row per day with device-level counts and a derived total visits column. Useful for daily traffic trends, joining to daily demographics, computing channel/device shares, or time-series aggregations. | Use for: Compare device type shares by day; Compute moving averages of daily traffic; Join daily device totals to demographics or page counters

views.name: daily_web_demographic_breakdown
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  day,
  'M' AS letter,
  'tw' AS shortcut,
  m_tw_cnt AS cnt,
  m_tw_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT
  day,
  'M' AS letter,
  'fb' AS shortcut,
  m_fb_cnt AS cnt,
  m_fb_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT
  day,
  'F' AS letter,
  'tw' AS shortcut,
  f_tw_cnt AS cnt,
  f_tw_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT
  day,
  'F' AS letter,
  'fb' AS shortcut,
  f_fb_cnt AS cnt,
  f_fb_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics
views.description: Unpivots the pre-aggregated web_demographics per day into one row per day x gender x channel with count and qty measures. Useful for demographic-level analysis, joining to channel/gender dims, or computing shares by gender/channel. | Use for: Time series of counts/quantities by gender and channel; Join demographics to channels_dim or gender_dim; Compute shares or growth by demographic segments

views.name: product_monthly_sales
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  mth,
  qty
FROM monthly_sales
views.description: Monthly sales per product preserving product and month with qty. Useful as the canonical monthly sales measure for trend analysis, joins to products or product_groups, and aggregations to higher levels. | Use for: Aggregate product sales over time windows; Compare actual sales to budget; Join to products/product_groups for rollups

views.name: product_latest_purchase
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.id AS id,
  p.purchased,
  p.brewery_id,
  p.qty,
  p.cost,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.product_id ORDER BY p.purchased DESC, p.id DESC) AS purchase_rank
FROM purchases p
views.description: Latest purchase event per product (one row per product) using purchased timestamp ordering. Exposes purchase-level measures and a purchase_rank so consumers can select top-N latest if desired. Useful for inventory recency, lead-time analysis, or joining most recent purchase metadata to products. | Use for: Find most recent purchase per product; Join recent purchase cost to inventory or product views; Compute recency-based supplier metrics

views.name: inventory_by_location_product
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.id,
  i.location_id,
  i.product_id,
  i.purchase_id,
  i.qty AS qty,
  l.warehouse AS warehouse,
  l.aisle AS aisle,
  l.position AS position,
  p.purchased AS purchased,
  p.brewery_id AS brewery_id
FROM inventory i
LEFT JOIN locations l ON l.id = i.location_id
LEFT JOIN purchases p ON p.id = i.purchase_id
views.description: Denormalized inventory rows with location, product and purchase metadata preserved. One row per inventory record. Useful for stock-level reporting, location-based pick optimization, and joining to purchases/products/locations. | Use for: Stock per warehouse/aisle/position; Age inventory using purchase.purchased; Compute location-level pick workloads

views.name: orders_with_line_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ol.id AS id,
  ol.order_id AS order_id,
  ol.product_id AS product_id,
  ol.qty AS qty,
  ol.amount AS amount,
  o.customer_id AS customer_id,
  o.ordered AS ordered,
  o.delivery AS delivery,
  c.name AS name
FROM orderlines ol
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.id = ol.order_id
LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
views.description: Order lines joined to orders and customers producing one row per orderline with order-level and customer info preserved. Useful for revenue calculations, customer order histories, and aggregations by customer or date. | Use for: Compute revenue by customer or date; Order-level fulfillment and delivery analysis; Join orderlines to product attributes

views.name: product_sales_with_product_info
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ms.product_id AS product_id,
  ms.mth AS mth,
  ms.qty AS qty,
  p.name AS name,
  p.group_id AS group_id,
  pg.name AS group_name
FROM monthly_sales ms
LEFT JOIN products p ON p.id = ms.product_id
LEFT JOIN product_groups pg ON pg.id = p.group_id
views.description: Monthly sales joined to product and product_group details. One row per product per month preserving product and group identifiers for rollups and labeling. | Use for: Sales rollup by product group; Trend charts with product names; Comparisons vs budget or minimums

views.name: picking_activity_with_employee
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  plog.picklist_id AS picklist_id,
  plog.log_time AS log_time,
  plog.activity AS activity,
  plog.location_id AS location_id,
  plog.pickline_no AS pickline_no,
  pl.created AS created,
  pl.picker_emp_id AS picker_emp_id,
  e.name AS name,
  e.title AS title
FROM picking_log plog
LEFT JOIN picking_list pl ON pl.id = plog.picklist_id
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.id = pl.picker_emp_id
views.description: Picking log events joined to picklist and employees (picker) where available. One row per picking_log event with picklist creation and picker employee preserved. Useful for pick performance, audit trails, and linking log events to responsible employees. | Use for: Analyze pick durations and activities; Link pick events to picker employees; Investigate anomalies in picking process
